exposure: severe iron-deficiency anaemia in pregnancy (haemoglobin < 8 g/dl)
cohort: The study included 212 pregnant women (106 with severe iron-deficiency anaemia and 106 controls with normal haemoglobin levels) from an inner-city London hospital.
finding: Severe iron-deficiency anaemia in pregnancy was associated with increased blood loss at delivery and higher rates of postpartum haemorrhage, but did not appear to influence other maternal or neonatal outcomes.
